config.title: font-display

intro.title: font-display
intro.body: In this lesson, you will learn to control how web fonts load and display using the CSS `font-display` property. You will build a simple webpage that applies different `font-display` values to custom fonts, observing how each setting affects the text rendering during loading. The core concept involves understanding font loading strategies like `swap`, `block`, and `fallback` to balance performance and user experience. You will work with CSS `@font-face` rules and the `font-display` property to implement these techniques.
intro.usecase: The font-display property is crucial for optimizing web performance in real-world applications where branding and typography are key. For example, e-commerce sites like Amazon or Shopify use custom fonts for product titles and branding, but need to prevent layout shifts while fonts load. News websites like The New York Times implement font-display to ensure article text appears immediately with fallback fonts, then smoothly transitions to their premium typefaces. This pattern is also essential in marketing landing pages and SaaS dashboards where maintaining visual consistency and fast perceived load times directly impacts user engagement and conversion rates.

objectives: Implement the font-display property in a CSS @font-face rule
Configure different font-display values (auto, block, swap, fallback, optional) for web fonts
Apply appropriate font-display strategies based on performance and user experience requirements
Manipulate font loading behavior to control text rendering during font downloads
Integrate font-display with existing font declarations to optimize page load
Construct CSS rules that balance font availability with content visibility
Update existing font implementations to include font-display for improved performance

steps.title: Create a CSS file and set up the HTML structure reference
steps.instruction: Create a new CSS file and add a comment that describes the HTML structure we'll be styling to demonstrate font loading behavior.
steps.hint: Start with a comment that outlines the HTML elements you'll be styling, such as headings and paragraphs.
steps.analogousExample:
/* HTML structure:

Main Title

Sample paragraph text.

Subheading

Another paragraph.

*/
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a CSS file with a comment that lists the HTML elements we'll style to learn about font-display.
successCriteria: A comment exists in the CSS file that describes the HTML structure with headings and paragraphs.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your comment clearly lists the HTML elements (headings and paragraphs) we'll be styling.
steps.feedbackWrong: Create a comment in your CSS file that describes the HTML structure with headings and paragraphs for our font-display demonstration.

steps.title: Define a custom font using @font-face
steps.instruction: Add an @font-face rule to import a custom font. Include font-family, src, and font-weight properties.
steps.hint: Use the @font-face rule to define a custom font. Specify the font-family name, the src URL (you can use a Google Fonts URL or a local path), and the font-weight.
steps.expectedOutcome: The CSS file now contains an @font-face rule that defines a custom font with font-family, src, and font-weight properties.
successCriteria: An @font-face rule is added with font-family, src, and font-weight properties defined.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your @font-face rule includes all required properties: font-family, src, and font-weight.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. Remember to use the @font-face rule with font-family, src, and font-weight properties.

steps.title: Apply the custom font to an element
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule to apply your custom font to an h1 heading element using the font-family property.
steps.hint: Create a selector for h1 and set font-family to the name you gave your font in the @font-face rule.
steps.expectedOutcome: The h1 heading will be styled with your custom font when the page loads.
successCriteria: An h1 selector with font-family property is added, referencing the custom font name.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've added a CSS rule for h1 with the font-family property set to your custom font name.
steps.feedbackWrong: The h1 element doesn't have the custom font applied. Check that you've created a CSS rule for h1 with the correct font-family value.

steps.title: Introduce the font-display property
steps.instruction: Add the font-display property to your existing @font-face rule and set its value to 'auto'.
steps.hint: The font-display property controls how a font is displayed while it's loading. The 'auto' value lets the browser use its default behavior.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your @font-face rule now includes the font-display property with the value 'auto'.
successCriteria: The @font-face rule contains a font-display property set to 'auto'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added 'font-display: auto;' inside your @font-face rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The font-display property with value 'auto' is missing from your @font-face rule. Add it to control font loading behavior.

steps.title: Use font-display: swap
steps.instruction: In your @font-face rule, change the font-display property value from 'auto' to 'swap'.
steps.hint: Look for the font-display property in your @font-face rule and replace its value with 'swap'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The font-display property in your @font-face rule is set to 'swap'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've changed the font-display property value to 'swap' within your @font-face rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't seem right. Look for the font-display property in your @font-face rule and change its value to 'swap'.

steps.title: Add a fallback font stack
steps.instruction: In your font-family declaration for the h1 element, add a fallback font stack after your custom font. Use a generic font family like 'sans-serif' as the final fallback.
steps.hint: Add a comma after your custom font name, then list fallback fonts like 'Arial, sans-serif'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The h1 element will now display fallback fonts while your custom font is loading, preventing invisible text.
successCriteria: The h1 selector includes a font-family property with your custom font name followed by at least one fallback font and a generic font family.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your font-family declaration includes your custom font name followed by fallback fonts like 'Arial, sans-serif'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The h1 element still doesn't have a complete font stack. Add fallback fonts after your custom font name in the font-family property.

steps.title: Try font-display: fallback
steps.instruction: Change the font-display value from 'swap' to 'fallback' in your @font-face rule.
steps.hint: Look for the font-display property in the @font-face rule and replace 'swap' with 'fallback'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The font-display property in the @font-face rule should now be set to 'fallback'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you changed 'swap' to 'fallback' in the font-display property within the @font-face rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The font-display property should be set to 'fallback' in the @font-face rule. Look for the line that says 'font-display: swap;' and change it to 'font-display: fallback;'.

steps.title: Compare different font-display values
steps.instruction: Add two more @font-face rules with different font-display values (block and optional) to compare loading behaviors.
steps.hint: Copy the existing @font-face rule and change the font-family name and font-display value for each new rule.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have three @font-face rules with different font-display values (swap, block, and optional) to compare their loading behaviors.
successCriteria: Two additional @font-face rules are added with font-display: block and font-display: optional values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but you need to add both font rules. Make sure you have one with font-display: block and another with font-display: optional.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't match what we need. You should add two more @font-face rules - one with font-display: block and another with font-display: optional. Each should have a unique font-family name.
